L196@P7: III. MONTE-CARLO SIMULATIONS OF OKLO REACTORS
L197@P7: To date, the Oklo uranium deposits are the only known place on Earth where two billion
L198@P7: years ago all conditions were appropriate for fission chain reactions. Those conditions are:
L199@P7: (i) a high concentration of uranium in different zones, with the 235U abundance being at
L200@P7: least 3%; (ii) a large amount of water in the pores and cracks of minerals, and; (iii) the
L201@P7: absence or near-absence of neutron poisons such as boron, lithium and the REEs. Elemental compositions and geometries of six Oklo zones were already reported at the first Oklo
L202@P7: symposium [11]. These data were enough to apply theories of neutron chain reactors [35]
L203@P7: to neutronic calculations for multiplication factors, neutron fluxes and other reactor physics
L204@P7: parameters. Naudet and Filip developed the multigroup code BINOCULAR [36], which
L205@P7: solved the neutron transport equations for some Oklo zones, especially the largest RZ2.
L206@P7: Interest in radioactive waste storage lead to the development of sophisticated deterministic
L207@P7: codes for modeling criticality and these have also been applied to Oklo [37, 38].
L208@P7: Most recently, a probabilistic approach based on the application of the code MCNP [39]
L209@P7: has been utilized. The MCNP code models neutron transport using Monte Carlo methods
L210@P7: and takes advantage of continuous libraries of energy dependent neutron cross sections. It
L211@P7: can deal with practically any realistic geometry of an active reactor core. Modeling with
L212@P7: MNCP has been performed for zones RZ2 [40, 41], RZ3 [42], RZ9 [43, 44], and RZ10 [41].
L213@P7: We illustrate some details of such modeling using the examples of zones RZ2 and RZ10.
